warmup.description: Activate posterior chain and prepare for hinge-dominant heavy lifting with dynamic mobility.
movements: Glute bridge march x 10 each side

main_exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
main_exercises.load_guidance: Heavy load at 8-9/10 effort, leaving 1 rep in reserve
main_exercises.form_cue: Push through the floor and keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift

main_exercises.name: Front Squat
main_exercises.load_guidance: Moderate-heavy load that challenges core and quad strength without losing posture
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep elbows high and torso upright as you descend

main_exercises.name: Step-Up (Dumbbell, High Box)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Choose a challenging load that allows controlled drive through the front leg
main_exercises.form_cue: Drive through the full foot and avoid pushing off the back leg

main_exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust (Paused)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a load that allows a 2-second pause at the top with strong contraction
main_exercises.form_cue: Hold the top position with full glute engagement before lowering

main_exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl (assisted if needed)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use assistance as needed to control the lowering phase fully
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep hips extended and control the descent as long as possible

main_exercises.name: Seated Calf Raises
main_exercises.load_guidance: Moderate load with full stretch at the bottom and pause at the top
main_exercises.form_cue: Move slowly and avoid bouncing between reps

cooldown.description: Release posterior chain tension and support recovery after heavy hinge work.
movements: Kneeling hip flexor stretch x 30s each side
Supine hamstring stretch x 30s each side

phase_notes.menstrual: Heavy hinge work like deadlifts may feel more demanding—consider reducing load or sets and focus on clean, controlled reps. Prioritize rest and avoid pushing to max effort.
phase_notes.follicular: Great phase to push heavy deadlifts and front squats—aim to increase load or improve rep quality. You may feel stronger and more explosive.
phase_notes.ovulatory: Peak strength and coordination make this ideal for heavy lifts—push intensity on deadlifts and step-ups while maintaining strong technique. Stay mindful of joint stability.
phase_notes.early_luteal: Maintain high effort but avoid going to failure—focus on consistent performance and controlled tempo, especially in eccentric-focused work like Nordics.
phase_notes.late_luteal: This session may feel very taxing—reduce volume or skip the most demanding elements like Nordics if needed. Focus on maintaining movement quality and stability.
